subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SRE 2410 - Review of Interim Financial Information
question: Under SRE 2410 'Review of Interim Financial Information Performed by the Independent Auditor of the Entity', what is the fundamental nature of procedures performed by the practitioner, and what form of assurance is expressed?
options: Procedures consist primarily of making inquiries (primarily of persons responsible for financial and accounting matters) and applying analytical and other review procedures; the practitioner expresses Moderate / Limited Assurance in negative form ('nothing has come to our attention...').
Procedures require 100% substantive vouching of all invoices; the practitioner expresses absolute assurance.
Procedures are identical to a statutory audit under SA 700; positive reasonable assurance is expressed.
The practitioner expresses no assurance and only stamps the trial balance.
ref: SRE 2410, Paragraphs 9 & 15 - Nature of Review Procedures and Form of Conclusion
explanation: Under SRE 2410, an interim review is substantially less in scope than an audit conducted in accordance with Standards on Auditing and does not enable the auditor to obtain assurance that the auditor would become aware of all significant matters. The procedures comprise inquiry and analytical procedures, yielding limited assurance expressed in negative form: 'Nothing has come to our attention that causes us to believe that the accompanying interim financial information does not give a true and fair view...'.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SAE 3400 - Examination of Prospective Financial Information (PFI)
question: Under SAE 3400 'The Examination of Prospective Financial Information', what is the vital distinction between a 'Forecast' and a 'Projection'?
options: A Forecast is PFI prepared on the basis of assumptions as to future events which management expects to take place (best-estimate assumptions); a Projection is PFI prepared on the basis of hypothetical assumptions about future events or a mixture of best-estimate and hypothetical assumptions ('what-if' scenarios).
A Forecast is prepared for 10 years, while a Projection is prepared for 1 month.
A Forecast is prepared by the auditor, while a Projection is prepared by the banker.
There is no distinction; both terms mean historical financial statements.
ref: SAE 3400, Paragraphs 3 & 4 - Definitions of Forecast and Projection
explanation: Under SAE 3400.3-4: (a) 'Forecast' means prospective financial information prepared on the basis of assumptions as to future events which management expects to take place and the actions management expects to take as of the date the information is prepared (best-estimate assumptions); (b) 'Projection' means prospective financial information prepared on the basis of hypothetical assumptions about future events and management actions, or a mixture of best-estimate and hypothetical assumptions.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SAE 3400 - Auditor's Opinion on Prospective Information
question: Can an auditor express an opinion that the results forecasted or projected in Prospective Financial Information (PFI) WILL BE ACHIEVED?
options: No. Under SAE 3400, the auditor cannot express an opinion as to whether the results will be achieved because events and circumstances frequently do not occur as expected and differences between actual results and PFI are often material.
Yes, if the auditor charges a success fee tied to the company's future profit.
Yes, provided management provides a counter-indemnity on judicial stamp paper.
Yes, if the forecast is prepared using automated artificial intelligence software.
ref: SAE 3400, Paragraph 9 - Inability to Express Opinion on Achievement of Results
explanation: Under SAE 3400.9, the auditor should not express an opinion on whether the results predicted in the PFI will be achieved. The auditor's examination report states whether anything has come to the auditor's attention to cause the auditor to believe that the assumptions do not provide a reasonable basis for the PFI, and provides an explicit warning that actual results are likely to differ from PFI.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SAE 3402 - Type 1 vs Type 2 Assurance Reports on Service Organizations
question: Under SAE 3402 'Assurance Reports on Controls at a Service Organization', what is the critical difference in the scope and period covered between a Type 1 and a Type 2 report?
options: A Type 1 report opines on the description and design suitability of service organization controls as of a specific date only; a Type 2 report opines on description, design suitability, AND operating effectiveness of controls throughout a specified period (ordinarily not less than 6 months).
Type 1 is issued by internal auditors, while Type 2 is issued by the High Court.
Type 1 covers cloud security, while Type 2 covers employee provident funds.
Type 1 is issued for private companies, while Type 2 is issued only for public banks.
ref: SAE 3402, Paragraph 9 - Type 1 and Type 2 Assurance Reports
explanation: Under SAE 3402.9: (1) Type 1 report: Report on description and design of controls at a service organization as of a specified point in time; (2) Type 2 report: Report on description, design suitability, AND operating effectiveness of controls throughout a specified period (typically 6 to 12 months), including detailed tests of controls and results.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SRS 4400 (Revised) - Agreed-Upon Procedures (AUP) Engagements
question: Under SRS 4400 (Revised) 'Engagements to Perform Agreed-Upon Procedures Regarding Financial Information', what form of assurance is expressed by the practitioner?
options: NO assurance is expressed; the practitioner merely issues a report of factual findings resulting from the specific procedures agreed with the engaging party, allowing users to draw their own conclusions.
Positive reasonable assurance (true and fair view).
Negative limited assurance ('nothing has come to our attention').
Absolute forensic certification.
ref: SRS 4400 (Revised), Paragraph 6 - Nature of Agreed-Upon Procedures Report
explanation: Under SRS 4400 (Revised).6, an agreed-upon procedures engagement involves performing procedures agreed between the practitioner and the engaging party and reporting factual findings. The practitioner does NOT express an audit opinion or review conclusion (i.e. zero assurance is expressed). Users of the report assess for themselves the procedures and findings and draw their own conclusions.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SRS 4410 (Revised) - Compilation Engagements
question: Under SRS 4410 (Revised) 'Compilation Engagements', what is the role and responsibility of the professional accountant in compiling financial statements for a client?
options: The practitioner applies accounting and financial reporting expertise to assist management in the preparation and presentation of financial information without undertaking to obtain any assurance on that information.
The practitioner audits all records and guarantees zero fraud in the compilation report.
The practitioner becomes a full partner in the client's business enterprise.
Compilation engagements can only be conducted by advocates enrolled in the Bar Council.
ref: SRS 4410 (Revised), Paragraph 5 - Objective of Compilation Engagement
explanation: Under SRS 4410 (Revised).5, the practitioner's objective in a compilation engagement is to apply accounting and financial reporting expertise to assist management in the preparation and presentation of financial information in accordance with an applicable financial reporting framework, without undertaking to obtain any audit or review assurance.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SAE 3420 - Pro Forma Financial Information in a Prospectus
question: Under SAE 3420 'Assurance Engagements to Report on the Compilation of Pro Forma Financial Information Included in a Prospectus', what is the practitioner's objective when examining pro forma financial statements for an IPO / Rights Issue?
options: Obtain reasonable assurance about whether the pro forma financial information has been compiled, in all material respects, by the responsible party on the basis of the applicable criteria and whether pro forma adjustments give appropriate effect to the specified event or transaction.
Predict whether the company's shares will list at a premium on the Bombay Stock Exchange.
Guarantee the future quarterly dividends of the company for the next 5 years.
Verify whether the underwriting syndicate has deposited the issue money in escrow.
ref: SAE 3420, Paragraph 6 - Purpose of Pro Forma Assurance Engagement
explanation: Under SAE 3420.6, the practitioner's objective is to obtain reasonable assurance about whether the pro forma financial information has been compiled, in all material respects, by the responsible party on the basis of the applicable criteria. This involves evaluating whether pro forma adjustments give appropriate effect to the transaction and whether the pro forma column reflects proper application of adjustments to unadjusted financial information.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Framework for Assurance Engagements - Elements of Assurance Engagement
question: Under the ICAI Framework for Assurance Engagements, which of the following lists the FIVE essential elements of any assurance engagement?
options: A three-party relationship (practitioner, responsible party, and intended users), an appropriate subject matter, suitable criteria, sufficient appropriate evidence, and a written assurance report.
An auditor, a lawyer, a banker, a police officer, and a judge.
Assets, Liabilities, Income, Expenses, and Equity.
Planning, Testing, Invoicing, Collection, and Archiving.
ref: ICAI Framework for Assurance Engagements - Paragraph 20 (Five Elements of Assurance)
explanation: Under the Framework for Assurance Engagements, every assurance engagement comprises five elements: (1) A three-party relationship involving a practitioner, a responsible party, and intended users; (2) An appropriate subject matter; (3) Suitable criteria; (4) Sufficient appropriate evidence; and (5) A written assurance report in the form appropriate to a reasonable assurance engagement or a limited assurance engagement.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SRE 2400 (Revised) - Engagements to Review Historical Financial Statements
question: Under SRE 2400 (Revised) 'Engagements to Review Historical Financial Statements', when can a practitioner accept a review engagement of financial statements?
options: When the practitioner determines that a review engagement would satisfy the intended purpose, ethical requirements including independence are met, and the preconditions for a review are present.
Only if the client's annual revenue is less than ₹10 Lakhs.
A review engagement can never be performed for historical financial statements.
Only if the practitioner is given power of attorney over the client's bank accounts.
ref: SRE 2400 (Revised), Paragraphs 29-31 - Acceptance of Review Engagements
explanation: Under SRE 2400 (Revised), a practitioner may accept a review engagement of historical financial statements when: (a) Ethical requirements, including independence, are complied with; (b) The practitioner has determined that a review engagement is appropriate; and (c) Preconditions for a review engagement are present (applicable reporting framework, management's agreement to responsibilities).

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Assurance on Sustainability & ESG Reporting (BRSR)
question: Under SEBI regulations, top 1,000 listed entities in India are required to furnish Business Responsibility and Sustainability Reporting (BRSR) Core, with mandatory reasonable assurance on specified ESG attributes. Which standard applies to assurance on non-financial sustainability reports?
options: SAE 3000 / ISAE 3000 (Revised) 'Assurance Engagements Other than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information' and SSAE 3000 issued by ICAI.
SA 700 'Forming an Opinion on Financial Statements'.
Section 44AB of the Income Tax Act, 1961.
CARO 2020 Clause (xxi).
ref: SEBI BRSR Core Mandate & ICAI Standard on Sustainability Assurance Engagements (SSAE 3000)
explanation: Assurance engagements on non-financial sustainability and ESG disclosures (including SEBI's BRSR Core) are governed by SSAE 3000 / ISAE 3000 (Revised) 'Assurance Engagements Other Than Audits or Reviews of Historical Financial Information', addressing greenhouse gas emissions, water usage, waste management, and gender diversity.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Reasonable Assurance vs Limited Assurance Engagements
question: What is the distinction in engagement risk and conclusion phrasing between a 'Reasonable Assurance' engagement and a 'Limited Assurance' engagement?
options: In reasonable assurance, engagement risk is reduced to an acceptably low level and conclusion is expressed in positive form ('in our opinion...'); in limited assurance, risk is reduced to an acceptable level that is meaningful but higher than reasonable assurance, and conclusion is expressed in negative form ('nothing has come to our attention...').
Reasonable assurance provides 100% insurance against insolvency, while limited assurance provides 50%.
Reasonable assurance is only for government entities, while limited assurance is for private citizens.
There is no difference in phrasing; both use identical positive certifications.
ref: ICAI Framework for Assurance Engagements - Paragraphs 11 & 12
explanation: Under the Framework for Assurance Engagements: (1) Reasonable assurance: Engagement risk is reduced to an acceptably low level; conclusion is expressed in a positive form; (2) Limited assurance: Engagement risk is reduced to a level that is acceptable in the circumstances of the engagement, but where that risk is greater than for a reasonable assurance engagement; conclusion is expressed in a negative form.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SRE 2410 - Management Representation in Interim Review
question: Under SRE 2410, what must the auditor obtain from management at the conclusion of an interim financial review?
options: Written representations confirming management's responsibility for design and implementation of internal controls, preparation of interim financial information, and disclosure of all fraud, uncorrected misstatements, and subsequent events.
A cash deposit equal to 3 months' professional fees.
An unconditional indemnity guaranteeing the firm against all civil litigation.
Written representations are prohibited in interim reviews.
ref: SRE 2410, Paragraph 34 - Written Representations in Interim Review
explanation: Under SRE 2410.34, the auditor should obtain written representation from management confirming: (a) Acknowledgement of its responsibility for designing and implementing internal control; (b) That interim financial information is prepared in accordance with the applicable framework; (c) That all uncorrected misstatements are immaterial; and (d) All known fraud or suspected fraud has been disclosed.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Attestation vs Direct Reporting Engagements
question: Under the Assurance Framework, what is the distinction between an 'Attestation Engagement' and a 'Direct Reporting Engagement'?
options: In an attestation engagement, a party other than the practitioner measures or evaluates the underlying subject matter against criteria and presents the subject matter information (which the practitioner then opines upon); in a direct reporting engagement, the practitioner directly measures or evaluates the underlying subject matter against criteria and reports the findings.
Attestation is only performed in courtrooms, while direct reporting is for television news.
Attestation engagements are always free of charge.
Direct reporting can only be performed by government intelligence agencies.
ref: ICAI Framework for Assurance Engagements - Attestation vs Direct Reporting
explanation: In an attestation engagement (e.g. audit of financial statements), management evaluates the subject matter (business transactions) against criteria (Ind AS) and presents subject matter information (financial statements), which the practitioner audits. In a direct reporting engagement (e.g. performance audit or greenhouse gas evaluation), the practitioner measures the underlying subject matter directly and presents the report.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SRE 2410 - Departure from Financial Reporting Framework
question: During an interim review under SRE 2410, the auditor discovers that the client has capitalized routine research expenses of ₹15 Crores in direct violation of Ind AS 38. If management refuses to correct the interim statements, what modification should the auditor issue in the review report?
options: A Qualified conclusion or Adverse conclusion (depending on materiality and pervasiveness), expressing that 'Except for / Because of the effects of the matter described in the Basis section, nothing has come to our attention...' or stating that the interim information does not give a true and fair view.
Issue an unmodified clean review report with an anonymous whistle-blower letter.
Automatically convert the review engagement into a criminal investigation under the IPC.
Resign without informing the Board or stock exchanges.
ref: SRE 2410, Paragraphs 36-39 - Departure from the Applicable Financial Reporting Framework
explanation: Under SRE 2410.36-39, if a matter has come to the auditor's attention that causes the auditor to believe that the interim financial information is materially misstated due to departure from the framework, and management refuses to adjust, the auditor shall modify the review report by issuing a Qualified conclusion or an Adverse conclusion.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SAE 3400 - Period Covered by Prospective Financial Information
question: Under SAE 3400, how should the practitioner evaluate the length of the period covered by prospective financial information?
options: The practitioner should consider the period of time for which prospective financial information can be reasonably prepared; as the period lengthens, assumptions become more speculative and the ability to formulate reliable best-estimate assumptions decreases.
The period must always be strictly 100 years.
Prospective information can only cover 7 days.
The period is fixed by the Ministry of Heavy Industries at exactly 25 years.
ref: SAE 3400, Paragraph 16 - Period Covered by Prospective Financial Information
explanation: Under SAE 3400.16, the auditor should consider the period of time covered by PFI. Assumptions become more speculative as the length of the period covered increases. As that period lengthens, the ability of management to formulate best-estimate assumptions decreases. Beyond a certain horizon (typically 3 to 5 years for most commercial entities), PFI loses reliability.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SRS 4400 - Distribution of AUP Report
question: Under SRS 4400 (Revised), to whom should the Agreed-Upon Procedures (AUP) report of factual findings be restricted in distribution?
options: The report is restricted to those parties that have agreed to the procedures to be performed, since others, unaware of the reasons for the procedures, may misinterpret the results.
The report must be published on billboards and social media platforms.
The report must be broadcast on national television.
The report can only be shown to members of the United Nations General Assembly.
ref: SRS 4400 (Revised), Paragraph 22 - Restriction on Distribution of AUP Report
explanation: Under SRS 4400.22, the report of factual findings is for the information of the engaging and specified parties only and is not to be used for any other purpose or to be distributed to any other parties. Because procedures are tailored to specific needs, third parties reading the findings without understanding the context might misinterpret the data.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SAE 3402 - User Auditor Reliance on Type 2 SOC Report
question: When a statutory auditor ('User Auditor') relies on a Type 2 SOC report issued by a service auditor under SAE 3402, what must the user auditor evaluate regarding the 'reporting period' of the Type 2 report?
options: Whether the period covered by the Type 2 report is appropriate for the user auditor's purposes, and whether adequate procedures have been performed for any intervening gap between the end of the service auditor's testing period and the user entity's balance sheet date.
The user auditor can accept any Type 2 report even if issued 10 years ago without checking the date.
The user auditor must ignore the Type 2 report and re-audit the service organization personally.
The user auditor must demand that the service organization pay their statutory audit fee.
ref: SA 402, Paragraph 17 & SAE 3402 - Evaluating Timing of Service Auditor's Tests
explanation: Under SA 402.17 and SAE 3402, when the service auditor's Type 2 report covers a period that does not coincide fully with the user entity's financial reporting period, the user auditor must evaluate whether the period tested provides sufficient appropriate evidence, and perform additional procedures (such as inquiry with service organization management or reviewing bridge letters) to cover the intervening gap.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SRS 4410 - Notice to Users in Compilation Engagements
question: In a compilation report issued under SRS 4410 (Revised), what explicit statement must the practitioner include to prevent users from mistaking the compilation for an audit?
options: A statement that since the compilation engagement is not an assurance engagement, the practitioner does not express an audit opinion or review conclusion on whether the financial statements are prepared in accordance with the applicable financial reporting framework.
A statement that the practitioner guarantees the financial statements are 100% free of fraud.
A statement that all company debts are backed by the personal assets of the practitioner.
A statement that the compilation report is valid for 100 years.
ref: SRS 4410 (Revised), Paragraph 40 - Required Statements in Compilation Report
explanation: Under SRS 4410 (Revised).40, the compilation report must include an explicit disclaimer stating that since a compilation engagement is not an assurance engagement, the practitioner is not required to verify the accuracy or completeness of the information provided by management, and accordingly does not express an audit opinion or a review conclusion.

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] Assurance on Greenhouse Gas (GHG) Statements (SAE 3410)
question: Under SAE 3410 'Assurance Engagements on Greenhouse Gas Statements', what are Scope 1, Scope 2, and Scope 3 emissions verified by the assurance practitioner?
options: Scope 1: Direct emissions from entity-owned or controlled sources; Scope 2: Indirect emissions from generation of purchased electricity, steam, heating, and cooling consumed; Scope 3: All other indirect emissions across the entire upstream and downstream value chain.
Scope 1: Factory smoke; Scope 2: Diesel generator fuel; Scope 3: Air conditioning refrigerant.
Scope 1: Corporate tax; Scope 2: GST; Scope 3: Customs duty.
Scope 1: Local sales; Scope 2: Interstate sales; Scope 3: Export sales.
ref: SAE 3410, Paragraph 14 - GHG Emissions Classification (Scope 1, 2, and 3)
explanation: Under SAE 3410 and the GHG Protocol: (1) Scope 1: Direct GHG emissions from operations owned or controlled by the entity (e.g. factory chimneys, company fleet); (2) Scope 2: Energy indirect emissions from purchased electricity, steam, or heating; (3) Scope 3: Other indirect emissions occurring in the value chain (upstream supply chain, business travel, product disposal).

subject: Advanced Auditing, Assurance and Professional Ethics
tag: [ICAI CA Final PYQ] SRE 2410 - Going Concern Consideration in Interim Review
question: During an interim review under SRE 2410, the auditor identifies material uncertainties that cast significant doubt upon the entity's ability to continue as a going concern. Management has adequately disclosed the uncertainty in the interim notes. What is the appropriate reporting by the auditor?
options: Express an unmodified conclusion and include an explanatory paragraph under the heading 'Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern' drawing attention to the relevant note in the interim financial information.
Express an Adverse conclusion automatically.
Refuse to issue any review conclusion until the full annual audit.
Require management to liquidate the company within 14 days.
ref: SRE 2410, Paragraphs 40-42 - Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern in Interim Review
explanation: Under SRE 2410.40-42, if adequate disclosure about the material uncertainty is made in the interim financial information, the auditor shall not modify the review conclusion, but shall include an explanatory paragraph under the heading 'Material Uncertainty Related to Going Concern' to highlight the matter, conforming to the principles of SA 570 (Revised).
